messages:
sam-sales: FYI ACME (enterprise POC) wants a temporary Dedicated pool capacity uplift next week for load testing. They need higher concurrency for 3 days and some extra burst credits. Can we do a short-term change?
anya-se: What numbers are they expecting? peak qps / tokens/sec / concurrency? Also which model are they targeting (gpt-4o / rwd-llama-70)?
acme-cto: Expecting ~120 qps at ~20 tokens/request, peak concurrency ~60. We'll test with rwd-llama-70 quantized. Need isolation — dedicated pool is required.
sam-sales: Thanks. They also want the uplift window Mon 2026-04-06 08:00 to Wed 2026-04-08 20:00 UTC.
tahir-engr: Ok rough math: 120 qps * 20 tokens = 2400 tokens/sec. With batching should be fine but need more instances to keep latency <200ms at peak. Suggest increasing pool min instances to 6 -> max 24 and add 50k burst credits for the window.
linh-sre: @tahir-engr can you propose the exact pool config change? I'll own the rollout and monitoring.
tahir-engr: Proposed CLI patch (will be applied as a one-off change):
```
# rwdctl CLI
rwdctl pools update --pool-id dp-acme-prod-poc \
  --min-instances 6 \
  --max-instances 24 \
  --burst-credits 50000 \
  --scale-policy manual \
  --expires-at 2026-04-08T20:00:00Z
```
add label `poc:acme-apr2026` for billing.
anya-se: That looks good. Two questions: 1) Does this impact other customers in the same region? 2) Do we need to reserve GPUs or just rely on burst capacity?
linh-sre: We'll provision within Dedicated capacity pool reserved for enterprise POCs in us-west-2. Should not affect hosted customers. We'll pin instances to the pool and the infra-bot will allocate nodes.
infra-bot: Provisioning request queued: req-98721. Allocating 4 GPUs now; remaining GPUs will be allocated on scale events. ETA for initial change ~ 18 minutes.
sam-sales: On pricing — can we keep this as a 'POC uplift' on Redwood side (no extra invoice) or do we need to bill them? ACME expects this to be included in POC terms.
anya-se: Finance checkpoint: we can offer one-time uplift as credit for up to 72 hours if legal signs the POC addendum. Need approval from finance. I'll ping finance and legal.
sam-sales: I'll attach the addendum to the deal.
acme-cto: Also need API keys for the dedicated pool test — token-level access preferably scoped to the pool. Is that possible?
linh-sre: Yes we can create scoped API key with pool restrictions and VPC egress allowed IPs. Send us the CIDR(s).
acme-cto: CIDR blocks: 203.0.113.0/24 and 198.51.100.0/28.
tahir-engr: Done. Also adding a short post-test cleanup playbook so we revert pool to baseline automatically at expiry.
anya-se: Can you paste the cleanup step?
tahir-engr: Cleanup snippet:
```
# revert to baseline
rwdctl pools update --pool-id dp-acme-prod-poc \
  --min-instances 2 \
  --max-instances 8 \
  --burst-credits 0 \
  --scale-policy balanced
```
I'll schedule at 2026-04-08T20:15:00Z.
linh-sre: I'll put temporary dashboards and alerts: p50/p95 latency, token/sec, GPU utilization, queue length. I'll also add a rollback runbook.
infra-bot: Provisioning complete for initial allocation. req-98721 -> success. Nodes: node-17, node-18, node-19, node-20.
sam-sales: Great. @acme-cto I'll share the scoped API key and instructions once legal confirms the POC addendum.
acme-cto: Thanks everyone. We'll run tests Tue-Wed and report results.
anya-se: Note for records: billing code `POC-ACME-APR2026`. Finance contact @anya-finance for final sign-off.
linh-sre: Scheduling the change for 2026-04-06 08:00 UTC. I'll post a short postmortem thread if anything unexpected happens. :thumbsup:
